critical.issue: IMPORT OF A VALID ENCRYPTED BACKUP IS ALWAYS REJECTED. A file produced by the system itself (downloaded via /backups/{file}/download, .archive.gz.enc) is refused with 400 'المحتوى ليس أرشيف mongodump مضغوطاً'. RCA: upload_backup() streams the body to a random temp path with NO extension and calls _inspect(scratch); _inspect derives `encrypted = path.endswith('.enc')` from that temp path, so an encrypted payload is never decrypted and the gzip magic check fails. Proof: the same archive uploaded UNencrypted (.archive.gz) is accepted (integrity=valid, storage=gridfs) — see tests test_valid_backup_accepted (fail) vs test_plaintext_archive_accepted_rca (pass). Fix: pass the original filename (or an explicit is_encrypted flag) into _inspect, e.g. name the scratch file with the uploaded extension.

rca_of_the_issue: Encrypted-backup import: enterprise.upload_backup() writes the multipart body to `{tempdir}/{uuid4().hex}` (no extension) and calls _inspect(scratch). _inspect() decides `encrypted = path.endswith('.enc')`, so for the extension-less scratch file it skips the openssl decryption step and reads the raw AES ciphertext, whose first two bytes are not 0x1f8b — hence the generic 'content is not a gzipped mongodump archive' rejection for a perfectly valid backup. Verified by uploading the decrypted plaintext of the very same archive, which is accepted (200, integrity=valid, storage=gridfs). Fix: name the scratch file with the uploaded suffix (or pass the encryption flag explicitly) before calling _inspect. Secondary issue: /bookings/{id}/financials returns 404 for bookings with non-ObjectId party references because db.oid() raises 404 on an InvalidId; the by_id() guard added to /bookings/{id}/full was not applied to finance.py.
